title: Gold leaf application on air-dry clay
subtitle: Applying imitation gold leaf to a sealed air-dry clay surface
excerpt: Imitation gold leaf gives air-dry clay pieces a bright metallic finish without firing or specialist glazes. A thin layer of size (water-based gilding adhesive) is applied to a sealed clay surface, the leaf is pressed on and brushed smooth, then a final sealer locks it in place. Works on any air-dry clay piece.
sourceNotes: Gilding technique derived from standard craft gilding methods.

glossaryTerms.definition: Water-based gilding adhesive that remains tacky for a controlled window after drying to allow leaf to stick

content.text: Gold leaf adheres to a dried clay surface via a water-based

that remains tacky in a predictable window. The leaf is pressed down onto the tacky size, then the excess is brushed away. Masking tape boundaries let you gild only selected areas for a deliberate design. The technique works on any bone-dry, sealed air-dry clay piece.

materials.name: Bone-dry air-dry clay piece, sealed with PVA

content.text: Ensure the clay piece is bone-dry and has been sealed with at least two coats of PVA. The PVA sealer is important: uncoated air-dry clay will absorb the size too quickly for the leaf to adhere.
Apply masking tape around any areas you want to protect from gilding. Press the tape edges firmly to prevent size bleeding underneath.

Paint a thin, even coat of water-based size onto the area to be gilded using the mop brush. Work into any textured recesses. Allow to dry for 15 to 20 minutes: the size should turn from milky to clear and feel tacky but not wet when touched with a knuckle.
Slide a sheet of leaf (still on its backing tissue) over the tacky surface and press the tissue gently from above. The leaf will transfer to the size. Peel the tissue away slowly.
Overlap the next sheet slightly to cover gaps. Continue until the whole area is covered. Do not worry about coverage gaps at this stage.
Once all leaf is applied, use the dry mop brush to press the leaf into any recessed areas and to brush away loose excess. Work gently in short strokes.

Apply one coat of water-based matte or satin varnish over the gilded area once the size has cured for 30 minutes. Varnish protects the leaf from tarnishing. Remove masking tape after the varnish coat dries.
Use silver, copper, or rose-gold leaf for a different metallic look. Gild only the rim of a bowl or the tips of a sculptured piece to add accent without full coverage.

items.problem: Leaf does not adhere and falls away in flakes
items.cause: The size was either not yet tacky or had already lost its tack window
items.fix: Check the size by touching with a knuckle: it should feel slightly sticky but leave no residue on your skin. If dry, apply fresh size and wait again. If wet, wait longer

items.problem: Leaf tarnishes quickly after a few days
items.cause: The varnish coat was not applied after gilding, leaving the imitation leaf exposed to air
items.fix: Apply water-based varnish over the gilded area as soon as the size is fully cured
